title: Metric Critique: Match Activity Volume
scenario: The BooedUp product team wants to measure whether the new AI Type Score model is increasing romantic connection activity on the platform.
prompt: The PM proposes tracking 'Total number of Match relationship initiations per day' as the critical metric for the Type Score model launch experiment. What is wrong with this metric, and what would be a better choice?
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Match the PAA terseness—'Should be normalized. [Better metric name] is better.'
expected_themes: cohort size differences mask true effect
Match initiation rate or mutual match rate
reference_answer: Should be normalized per daily active user. Match Initiation Rate (initiations per DAU) is better.

grading_rubric.description: Answer explicitly states the metric is not normalized, or is a count/volume metric when a rate is needed
Answer names a per-user or per-interaction rate metric (e.g., Match Initiation Rate, initiations per DAU, initiations per profile view)
Answer mentions cohort size, DAU variance, or experiment group comparability as the reason normalization matters

hints: Think about how you compare two experiment groups with different numbers of users.
A count metric can grow just because more users joined, not because behavior improved.
What would happen if the treatment group had 10% more daily active users than control?
common_mistakes: Proposing 'mutual match rate' without noting the flaw is lack of normalization (mutual match rate IS normalized, but doesn't address the original flaw)
Criticizing the metric for not measuring outcomes (e.g., 'should measure messages sent') when the real flaw is it's a volume count
Overcomplicating the answer—PAA style is one terse sentence
